blogs.title: MODY Red Flags: When Early-Onset Hyperglycaemia Isn’t Type 1 or Type 2
blogs.description: This post distills the bedside clues that should trigger suspicion for HNF1A-MODY in young adults: early-onset diabetes across generations, absence of ketosis, negative islet autoantibodies, preserved endogenous insulin secretion, and marked postprandial hyperglycaemia on OGTT. We highlight how rising obesity blurs the classic phenotype and why BMI or metabolic syndrome alone cannot rule out MODY. Practical takeaways include how to prioritize MODY in the differential and avoid misclassification that delays the right therapy.

blogs.title: Stimulated C-peptide in the MODY Workup: Supportive, Not Definitive
blogs.description: Using the case’s glucagon-stimulated C-peptide (0.83 nmol/L) as a springboard, we review how to interpret fasting and stimulated C-peptide when differentiating MODY from type 1 diabetes. We discuss assay caveats, timing relative to diagnosis, and the risk of false reassurance early in autoimmune disease. The post outlines a pragmatic triage: who merits genetic testing, where the Exeter MODY calculator fits, and why calibration issues in non-European populations mean clinicians must not over-rely on a single tool.

blogs.title: Treating HNF1A-MODY in 2026: Sulfonylurea Tradition vs GLP-1 Pragmatism
blogs.description: Therapeutics through the lens of this case: initial insulin for severe hyperglycaemia, then safe de-intensification after genetic confirmation. We compare sulfonylureas (historic first-line) with GLP-1 receptor agonists for durability, hypoglycaemia risk, weight effects, and patient preference, referencing crossover data (glimepiride vs liraglutide). We also touch on the role of metformin and DPP-4 inhibitors as adjuncts, and propose an algorithm for choosing therapy based on A1c, hypoglycaemia risk, and beta-cell reserve.

blogs.title: SGLT2 Meets HNF1A: Why Glycosuria Is a Clue—and SGLT2 Inhibitors May Backfire
blogs.description: HNF1A regulates renal SGLT2 expression, lowering the renal threshold for glucose and producing glycosuria that can outpace the degree of hyperglycaemia—a diagnostically useful pearl. We review the hazards of adding pharmacologic SGLT2 inhibition in HNF1A-MODY: dehydration, euglycaemic DKA, and potential hemodynamic compromise, with a practical risk–benefit framework. The post offers counseling tips and alternative strategies for patients who present with prominent glycosuria.

blogs.title: Calling a Novel Variant Pathogenic: From ACMG Criteria to Clinical Action
blogs.description: Using the novel HNF1A c.809A>G (p.N270S) variant, we walk through a clinician’s approach to variant interpretation: domain context (DNA-binding), segregation with disease, absence from population/databases, in-silico support (e.g., AlphaMissense), and how this maps to ACMG to reach a likely pathogenic call. We discuss communicating uncertainty, avoiding over- or under-calling VUS, and how a confident classification justifies therapeutic de-intensification and cascade family testing.

blogs.title: Early Autonomic Neuropathy in MODY? Making Sense of Abnormal Sudomotor Tests
blogs.description: The case’s severely reduced sudomotor function raises questions about small-fiber involvement early in HNF1A-MODY. We review what electrochemical skin conductance actually measures, its sensitivity/specificity, and how hyperglycaemia alone can drive early autonomic findings. The post offers a rational approach to screening and follow-up when sudomotor testing is abnormal despite short diabetes duration, including when (and when not) to change management.
